title: Compare
concept: Compare numbers with >, <, == and != to make a condition

steps.say: This cell holds 4 gems. The robot should leave exactly 2.
`while gems_here():` only asks "any gems?", so it takes all 4.
`gems_here() > 2` asks a sharper question: is the count more than 2?
Run it. A comparison is True or False, like a sensor.
Use it as the condition. The loop stops when the answer turns False.
`<` means less than. This adds gems until there are 6. Also: `==` equal, `!=` not equal.
After `move()`, add `while gems_here() > 1:` with `pick()` inside. Not `if`: piles need several picks.
The start cell counts too. Trim it before the walk.
Run it. If whole piles vanish, check the number after `>`.

guided.done: One gem left on every pile, whatever its size.

recap.say: A comparison is a condition: `while gems_here() > 1:` repeats while the count is more than 1.

big_piles_only: Compare your result with the Goal view: which piles should stay?
Decide once per cell with `if gems_here() > 2:`, then clear that pile with a `while`.
level_piles: Look at the Goal view: every cell ends with 2 gems, even empty ones.
Two loops on each cell: `while gems_here() < 2:` adds, `while gems_here() > 2:` takes.
